# V139 reviewed Functions baseline

Current baseline: `6eb34420c0883bec08aba98206aa1df080e37755`, reviewed rejection-cycle and terminal-page identity release.
Only `jarvis-semantic-planner.js` changes inside Functions. A rejected query now
passes a typed decision receipt into recovery and the next decision. It remains
non-operational, cannot satisfy a goal, and excludes only the exact proposal
under unchanged instruction, model, actor/mission identity and observed evidence.
New source/record dependencies reopen the review. History is engine-owned,
bounded, and never prunes an entire collection for one rejected projection.

Terminal cursor deduplication normalizes only a template actually submitted for
an authenticated receipt and that receipt's concrete route. It no longer compares
those aliases literally. Changing projection/page size cannot rerun that empty
page. A different organization, cursor, filters or source remains separate.
The runtime's completeForQuery=false terminal receipt stays unchanged and cannot
prove population or objective completion.

A reduced regression from the actual 92c83bf2 Chrome trace failed before the fix
at recovery's missing typed receipt. It now exercises proposal, semantic rejection,
recovery and the next decision without a repeated query review. Another test
executes the real runtime with a simulated Firestore boundary, then exercises
both pre-inference cursor pruning and the planner's post-selection deduplication.
Neither is represented as physical Chrome certification. All 307 focused checks
and 1,999 full-root checks pass, with zero failures and two environment skips.
Independent success/closure reviews remain tested and required.

The preceding physical Chrome run ended PARTIAL, PLANNER_UNAVAILABLE: 25 local
calls, 210,209 ms from submission to native final, 98,299 ms in completion audits.
Only one source read and one empty scoped query executed. Repeated rejected
proposals were not operational reads. This is not a successful certification.
Fresh local physical search, CI and the complete clean Chrome mission remain
required. No model, provider, permissions or operational data changes.
The explicit ancestor-checked fail-closed guard remains intact.

## Previous exact-source baseline


Current baseline: `56099aec8d355deec9ec3c0dd50ca51add647fbc`, reviewed exact-source evidence release.

or filter values to that query. Legacy single-collection field receipts retain
their unambiguous field ownership. Exact authenticated template resolutions
remain usable; no new tenant, domain or operational permissions are introduced.

Coverage source citations are constrained to authenticated queries of that exact
route or its recorded template resolution. Technical scope facts identify both
requested and resolved routes. Query exhaustion still cannot satisfy a goal;
all independent objective coverage and closure checks remain enforced.

Both new regressions fail on the preceding source. All 304 focused checks and
1,996 full-root checks pass, with zero failures and two explicit environment
skips. VM-based review tests execute the real collection-identity dependency.
The previous actual Chrome mission ended PARTIAL after 58 local semantic calls;
that is neither success nor an external blocker. A fresh deployed Chrome mission
is still required. No operational writes, model changes or external AI calls.
The explicit ancestor-checked fail-closed Functions guard is retained.

## Previous pending-evidence baseline


Current baseline: `850794d464722af1a187066d1d03a858ba279296`, the reviewed pending-evidence decision release.
Only `jarvis-semantic-planner.js` changes inside Functions. A still-pending goal
with a validated novel next action no longer triggers independent negative
coverage/scope reviews before that action. Its partial references and missing
scopes stay pending. A positive claim, a changed accredited positive proof, or
an attempted stop still receives independent review; code and query exhaustion
never certify operational objectives. Negative client assessments cannot prune
sources. Fresh engine-owned source exclusions now apply to the single immediate
recovery decision, not just the following iteration.

The fresh Chrome trace at the previous release reached another relevant module
but was explicitly aborted for performance diagnosis after 42 local model calls;
it was not a successful mission or an external blocker. Replay of that exact
pending/new-source request with a controlled model boundary reproduces the old
pre-decision negative review, while this release preserves a grounded query in
two stages and keeps all three objectives pending. No operational tool executes
in that replay. Four combinations of new records/schema and relationship/temporal
goals use one decision; success/stop and immediate recovery exclusions remain
covered by separate tests.

All 302 focused checks pass. The full existing root suite has 1,988 PASS and
zero failures, with two explicit environment skips. Six general source/cycle
regressions pass separately and are included in the existing CI test command.
Fresh CI, physical search, aligned release and the complete clean Chrome mission
remain required. No model, provider, permission or operational data changes.
The guard remains explicit, ancestor-checked and fail-closed.

against every future Functions change. All 277 focal checks and 1,933 local
full-suite checks passed with zero failures. The one Linux-only browser check
and Firestore emulator checks require fresh CI verification before closure.

## Initial workflow repair baseline

The initial workflow repair used `.github/scripts/v139-functions-guard.mjs` and the
explicit baseline `7f50f7d306f789a8dbde355435895b8d54abb872`. This is the integrated
branch HEAD before this workflow-only repair, not a dynamically accepted HEAD.
Platform CI run https://github.com/heberzzt-wq/fixgo-app/actions/runs/38281211531
passed at that exact SHA. This accepts already integrated Functions history;
it does **not** certify the canonical real reel or the unfinished local planner work.

## Why the previous base stopped working

The original August workflow isolated a frontend/bridge reel change from Functions
changes. Commit `36b13c88f74d5504384f203b58a928c896ea99db` explicitly rebased the
guard to an accepted head. Commit `78f2dd6e1984d1ccc392bae961d70238ad20484e`
advanced only Windows to `dbe0a94b660008d4620f9ce4726ca66b2a5db555`, a September 17
workflow commit restoring dispatch-only certification. It was a frozen accepted
branch snapshot, not a Functions dependency or immutable reel contract. Linux
subsequently retained `45c9231715ad1d8f50756328c6e4128deebba581` instead.
Both historical comparisons eventually rejected legitimate integrated evolution.
Run https://github.com/heberzzt-wq/fixgo-app/actions/runs/38101666190 failed at the
Windows guard and never ran the real mission or its marker.

Personnel, identity, crew, financial/service authorization and their tests belong
to integrated B2B/B2C functionality, not a new change introduced by this reel
certification. The generated platform contract follows that platform evolution.
Package additions include the biometric Human/TensorFlow/JPEG dependencies.
Secure entry and its aliases retire historical independent generator/withdrawal
authority and route callers to canonical security handlers.

The semantic planner and repository planner **are relevant to reel behavior**:
they must not be declared harmless merely because their changes are legitimate.
`index.js` and `jarvis-intent-runtime-v7.cjs` also retire cloud semantic authority
in favor of local-only Jarvis. The canonical script imports the semantic planner
directly and still constructs a Google/Vertex provider. Thus compatibility with
the current local-only policy, provider credentials, media generation and the
actual reel result remain subject to the real mission, not this guard.

The baseline deliberately includes this integrated history without reverting it.
It does not exempt any file from future review: **all** committed Functions
additions, removals, renames and modifications after the baseline still fail.
Any future legitimate Functions release needs an explicit reviewed baseline
advance with corresponding CI evidence; never substitute HEAD/event-before
automatically. A missing baseline, non-ancestor baseline, Git error, wrong branch,
or tracked/untracked Functions worktree change fails closed as well. Ignored
installed dependencies do not count as source changes.

## Certification and execution boundaries

The main workflow now runs `certify-v139` on push or manual dispatch, without
external credentials or a live provider call. All its existing syntax, focal,
business and full-CI checks remain; guard regressions are also run explicitly.
Its marker identifies local **compatibility tests only**, not an Ollama end-to-end
mission. This change neither installs nor selects another semantic model.

The former Windows job is retained in
`.github/workflows/v139-legacy-external-reel.yml`, with the same bridge/canonical
mission step and Windows certification marker. Its only trigger is manual
`workflow_dispatch`, gated by `authorize_paid_external_reel == true`; the boolean
input defaults to false and explicitly warns about Google/Vertex and Runpod usage
and potential charges. There is no push, schedule, workflow-call or downstream-run
trigger. No historical external mission is authorized or executed for this repair.
No marker executes following a guard or mission failure. Neither workflow suppresses
failures with `continue-on-error` or equivalent constructs.

An opt-in historical result is provider compatibility evidence, not certification
of the workstation's single Qwen3.5:9b/Ollama model. The current local mission and
unfinished planner work still require their separate real Chrome certification.
The other legacy canonical workflows are outside this repair; their push filters
do not match the files changed here and no workflow-run hook was found.
